topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's objectives, reviewing the hallmarks of cancer and the genetic progression of tumors.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and oncogenic signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases, deregulate growth control and drive cell proliferation.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how differentiation arrest contributes to malignancy, using examples from hematopoiesis, leukemias, and intestinal crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Apoptosis resistance, replicative immortality, and p53 tumor suppression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells bypass apoptosis, senescence, and telomere shortening through p53 pathway deregulation and telomerase reactivation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address metabolic rewiring in cancer cells, including the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how tumors switch on blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and obtain nutrients for growth.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and circulating tumor cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metastatic cascade from local tissue invasion and circulation tracking to seed-and-soil colonization and metastatic genomics.

topics.label: Concluding remarks and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarising the hallmarks and previewing upcoming practical sessions.
